_doc: McCready's Opera House (#1143): the building lab's step 2, the spec on its lot, written by tools/buildings/opera_house_spec.py (edit it, not this). NOT BUILT: the build waits for after the slice; keys marked NEW are parts the builder doesn't have (experiments/building_lab/opera_house/README.md). Sizes here, the look on the sheet (experiments/building_lab/opera_house/sheet).

identity.owner: Ezra McCready, who sold his share in the Argentine lode in 1880 and built the town something to be proud of (and a stage for his wife's sister)
identity.trade: an opera house: travelling companies, melodrama, a singer with the band, lectures, the magic lantern, the Fourth of July ball, the Miners' Union meetings
identity.means: the only brick building in Salt Creek but the bank: freighted-in brick, plate glass, iron, a hundred opera chairs from Chicago, scenery painted in Denver
identity.age_and_repair: 1 year: the brick new and sharp, the walk already worn at the doors; one lane window boarded where a drunk put a bottle through

lot._doc: valley.json town.north (NEW lot, added at the build, not before: a valley change can tip the card-game tests): past the undertaker's (x 106-128) a lane x 128.0-130.4 (8 ft: the hall's west exits), the lot x 130.4-149.0 by the town's 125 ft depth to Back Street; Main Street's and Back Street's x [-125, 130] grow to 150. The East Road still leaves from (130, 0) south-east, clear of the walk. The building's origin its EAST front corner (facing 180). The ground (ValleyTerrain.height, 2026-11-24): -0.44 (west) to -0.58 (east) at the front line, +0.18..+0.06 at 20 m back, +0.84..+0.38 at 30 m (Back Street's bank): a pad dug level at the walk's street edge (y -0.5) under the building and its yard, a bank left behind.

walk.why: A brick front needs no awning; three wide stone-edged steps across the three doorways for a crowd and ladies' skirts.

levels._doc: The hall's floor at the walk's top; the stage, the dressing block and the lower boxes 3 ft 6 in over it; the foyer and the balcony's back aisle 5 m over it (the lobby 16 ft high); the scene loft over the foyer; the hall's trusses on the plate 10 m over the floor, its plaster ceiling under them (32 ft); the stage house's gridiron 30 ft over the stage. NEW levels: stage, attic, dress_upper, dress_roof, front_roof, box (the builder knows cellar, ground and upper).

box._doc: the boxes and their passages, 3.5 m over the stage

frame._doc: A load-bearing brick building, timber floors and roof. Brick walls by Kidder (public halls: 17 in to the upper floor, 13 in above; 13 in for the fire wall and the dressing block), lime mortar, on sandstone footings 4 ft down (below Colorado's frost). Joists by the Wood Handbook's working stresses (yellow pine, 1,200 lb/in2 bending; deflection L/360), 100 lb/ft2 where a crowd stands (Kidder's for theatres), 70 the dance floor, 40 the lofts and roofs (snow). `--sizing` prints each (the README's table). Dressed sizes, metres [width, depth].

stone_wall._doc: NEW use: the jail's stone walls laid as BRICK (`masonry` brick; BrickWall, the README's parts): members as lifts of nine courses (0.6 m, the jail's course) and 1.2 m long, so the walls are ~2,000 members, not 100,000 bricks; chips by the voxel carving, a charge drops lifts. Common bond (a header course every sixth), 8 x 4 x 2 1/4 in bricks, 3/8 in joints: the shader's. Dressed buff sandstone: the quoins, the base course, sills, keystones over the arches, the coping.

balcony._doc: NEW (`Balcony` kind `straight`, the README's parts): the deck in tiers stepped 0.3 m (each tier a floor of its own on raking carriages: 3x12 at 16 in from the rail beam up to the lobby's back wall, 9 ft), the rail beam 8x14 on three cast-iron columns (6 in, 3/4 in metal; the outer two the box passages' beams' too), a panelled gilt fascia on the rail's line with a velvet-padded rail 0.75 m over the front row; 100 lb/ft2. Each row 18 seats with a step down at either end. The columns stand in the parquet's middle and side aisles on brick piers. Clear under the rail: 4.0 m (standing room).

boxes._doc: NEW (`Balcony` kind `box`): two private boxes (Sean, 2026-11-26, #1244: one a side, 'John Wilkes Booth' style for an assassination, #1287), over the forestage's ends either side of the proscenium, floor 3.5 m over the stage. Each is shut off from the house: reached only from the balcony's back aisle through its vestibule door (it opens in; a bar drops into iron keepers on the passage side) and along its own passage, 0.9 m wide, plastered and papered, on the hall's side wall, to the box's door (a gimlet hole in it) in the box's back wall. The box: 1.6 x 2.4 m, four gilt chairs, a curtain on a rod and a padded rail on the house side; joists 3x10 from the side wall to the front beam, its front corner on a cast-iron column. A man in the box can come up behind the guest unseen, shoot, and go over the rail to the forestage (3.5 m: a sprain or a broken leg), through the door under the box into the wings and out the stage door to the yard; or back along the passage to the balcony and down the stairs.
